{{Short description|French mathematician}}
'''Jean Ville''', also known under the names Jean-André Ville et André Ville, born 24 June 1910 in [[Marseille]], died 22 January 1989 in [[Blois]], was a French mathematician. He is known for having proved an extension of [[von Neumman's minimax theorem]], as well as contributions in the fields of statistics and economics. He was one of the pioneers of the theory of [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingale]]s.<ref>{{cite journal
 | language = en
 |first = Glenn|last =  Shafer
 | title = The education of Jean André Ville
 | journal = Electronic Journal for History of Probability and Statistics 
 | volume = 5 | number = 1 | date= June 2009 | pages = 1–50 | issn =
 | url = http://www.jehps.net/juin2009/Shafer.pdf}}, page 5.</ref>

== Life ==
Jean André Ville was the son of Jean Baptiste Ville (1871-1927) and Marie Vernet (1876-1955), both from families from [[Mosset]] in [[Pyrénées-Orientales]].<ref name = hdm >Jean Pares, [http://www.histoiredemosset.fr/mossetpdf/n61_ville_mai_2008.pdf '' Jean André Ville (1910-1989) mathematician. Le savant de Mosset ''].</ref> His first name was that of his godfather and uncle, Jean Ville, the second, that of his grandfather, André Vernet. André was the first name used in the family, but in his professional life, he used Jean. [[Bernard d'Orgeval]], a classmate, writes in the directory of former students of the ENS 1992 "very discreet about his private life, discretion marked by the use of the first name Jean in his scientific and administrative career, while in the family he was André".<ref name = hdm />

He was a former student of the [[lycée Thiers]] of [[Marseille]] and the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] (Promo 1929), of which he entered first.<ref>He was first eligible, but fifth on admission. He became [[cacique]] following the resignation of the four candidates who preceded him. {{Harvsp | Shafer | 2009 | p = 2}}.</ref>

[[Ville's inequality]] is named for him, after he proved it in 1939.<ref>{{cite thesis
 | first1=Jean | last1=Ville
 | title=Etude Critique de la Notion de Collectif
 | year=1939
 | url=http://www.numdam.org/item/THESE_1939__218__1_0.pdf
 }}</ref>

== Publications ==
* ''Applications de la théorie des probabilités aux jeux de hasard'', d'[[Émile Borel]] et Jean Ville (1938)
